targets Rubin (<code>sm_107</code>)</td></tr>\r\n</table>\r\n\r\nFor more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release.\r\n\r\n# Backwards Incompatible Changes\r\n\r\n## torch.nn\r\n\r\n- `torch.nn.LinearCrossEntropyOptions` no longer accepts `acc_policy=\"balanced\"`; use `\"compact\"` instead (#188283)\r\n\r\n  The `\"balanced\"` policy was removed because `\"compact\"` provides the same weight-gradient accumulation precision with lower memory use on CUDA, already uses the equivalent scratch layout for mixed-precision inputs on other devices, and was never selected by `\"auto\"`. Constructing the options with `acc_policy=\"balanced\"` now raises `ValueError: invalid acc_policy: 'balanced'; expected one of 'auto', 'accurate', 'compact'`.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  options = torch.nn.LinearCrossEntropyOptions(acc_policy=\"balanced\")\r\n  loss = torch.nn.functional.linear_cross_entropy(\r\n      input, linear_weight, target, options=options\r\n  )\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  options = torch.nn.LinearCrossEntropyOptions(acc_policy=\"compact\")\r\n  loss = torch.nn.functional.linear_cross_entropy(\r\n      input, linear_weight, target, options=options\r\n  )\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Autograd\r\n\r\n- Clamp and min/max boundary subgradients now follow the selected dispatcher schema's input space (#191142)\r\n\r\n  This affects gradients exactly at nondifferentiable bounds or ties. A scalar clamp bound is a fixed parameter, so the input gradient at equality changes from `1` to the minimum-norm subgradient `0`. A Tensor bound is part of the differentiable input space, so `clamp`, `clamp_min`, and `clamp_max` now split the gradient evenly between the input and bound at an ordinary tie instead of assigning it entirely to the input. `fmin` and `fmax` use the same even tie split, and forward-mode AD for the min/max family is aligned with these rules. Code that intentionally depends on the old tie-breaking behavior can express it explicitly with `torch.where`, such as `torch.where(value >= bound, value, bound)`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch\r\n\r\n  x = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  torch.clamp_min(x, 0.0).backward()\r\n  print(x.grad)  # tensor(1.)\r\n\r\n  value = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  bound = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  torch.clamp_min(value, bound).backward()\r\n  print(value.grad, bound.grad)  # tensor(1.) tensor(0.)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch\r\n\r\n  x = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  torch.clamp_min(x, 0.0).backward()\r\n  print(x.grad)  # tensor(0.)\r\n\r\n  value = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  bound = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)\r\n  torch.clamp_min(value, bound).backward()\r\n  print(value.grad, bound.grad)  # tensor(0.5000) tensor(0.5000)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n- Custom Python process groups that implement `new_group()` must now accept a `backend` keyword argument (#188489)\r\n\r\n  This applies when the default process group supplies its own `new_group()` method and `torch.distributed.new_group()` delegates subgroup creation to it. PyTorch now forwards the resolved backend so custom implementations can construct the requested subgroup correctly. Existing implementations without this parameter will raise `TypeError: ... got an unexpected keyword argument 'backend'`. Accept and use the argument, or accept and ignore it when the implementation has only one backend.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  class MyProcessGroup(...):\r\n      def new_group(\r\n          self, ranks, *, timeout=None, pg_options=None,\r\n          group_name=None, group_desc=None\r\n      ):\r\n          ...\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  class MyProcessGroup(...):\r\n      def new_group(\r\n          self, ranks, *, timeout=None, backend=None, pg_options=None,\r\n          group_name=None, group_desc=None\r\n      ):\r\n          ...\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- NCCL symmetric-memory pools no longer automatically upgrade segments allocated after `register_mem_pool(..., symm=True)` to symmetric windows (#192112)\r\n\r\n  Registering those late segments from the CUDA allocator callback could invoke a collective NCCL operation on only some ranks while holding the allocator lock, causing an unrecoverable hang. Late segments now remain ordinary registered NCCL buffers. Applications that need newly allocated segments to use symmetric-window algorithms must collectively deregister and register the pool again after those allocations are created.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  backend.register_mem_pool(pool, symm=True)\r\n  with torch.cuda.use_mem_pool(pool):\r\n      tensor = torch.empty(size, device=\"cuda\")\r\n  # Newly allocated segments were automatically upgraded, but this could hang.\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  backend.register_mem_pool(pool, symm=True)\r\n  with torch.cuda.use_mem_pool(pool):\r\n      tensor = torch.empty(size, device=\"cuda\")\r\n\r\n  # Collectively refresh registration after the pool grows.\r\n  backend.deregister_mem_pool(pool)\r\n  backend.register_mem_pool(pool, symm=True)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Nonmember ranks now receive `GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER` instead of `None` from experimental `torch.distributed.split_group()` (#190725)\r\n\r\n  When the calling rank is absent from every requested split, `split_group()` now returns the same nonmember sentinel as `new_group()`. Code that identifies nonmembers with `is None` must compare against `torch.distributed.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER` instead.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  group = torch.distributed.split_group(\r\n      split_ranks=[[0, 1], [2, 3]]\r\n  )\r\n  if group is None:\r\n      return\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  group = torch.distributed.split_group(\r\n      split_ranks=[[0, 1], [2, 3]]\r\n  )\r\n  if group == torch.distributed.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER:\r\n      return\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Linear Algebra Frontend\r\n\r\n- Remove the deprecated `torch.cholesky()` and `Tensor.cholesky()` APIs (#186817)\r\n\r\n  Calls now raise a `RuntimeError` directing users to `torch.linalg.cholesky()`. The replacement returns a lower-triangular factor; callers that previously requested `upper=True` should take the conjugate transpose with `.mH`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  lower = torch.cholesky(a)\r\n  upper = torch.cholesky(a, upper=True)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  lower = torch.linalg.cholesky(a)\r\n  upper = torch.linalg.cholesky(a).mH\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Remove the deprecated `torch.qr()` and `Tensor.qr()` APIs (#186815)\r\n\r\n  Calls now raise a `RuntimeError` directing users to `torch.linalg.qr()`. Replace the Boolean `some` argument with `mode=\"reduced\"` or `mode=\"complete\"`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  q, r = torch.qr(a)\r\n  q_full, r_full = torch.qr(a, some=False)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  q, r = torch.linalg.qr(a, mode=\"reduced\")\r\n  q_full, r_full = torch.linalg.qr(a, mode=\"complete\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Profiler\r\n\r\n- The deprecated `use_cuda` argument has been removed from `torch.profiler.profile` and `torch.autograd.profiler.profile` (#192543)\r\n\r\n  Passing `use_cuda` to either profiler now raises `TypeError: profile.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_cuda'`. Select CUDA explicitly through `activities` when using `torch.profiler.profile`, or use `use_device=\"cuda\"` with `torch.autograd.profiler.profile`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.profiler.profile(use_cuda=True) as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n\r\n  with torch.autograd.profiler.profile(use_cuda=True) as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.profiler.profile(\r\n      activities=[\r\n          torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU,\r\n          torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA,\r\n      ]\r\n  ) as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n\r\n  with torch.autograd.profiler.profile(use_device=\"cuda\") as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Dynamo\r\n\r\n- The `tvm` backend now uses TVM's relax frontend exclusively; the relay path has been removed (#190766, #189639)\r\n\r\n  Relay was removed in TVM 0.20, so the backend now requires a TVM providing `tvm.relax.frontend.torch`. Two things are gone with it: the relay-only `scheduler` / `trials` options, replaced by a TVM pipeline passed as `options={\"pipeline\": ...}`; and the `tvm_meta_schedule` / `tvm_auto_scheduler` backend entry points, which no longer exist in `torch._dynamo.backends.tvm`. With an older TVM installed, `torch.compile(..., backend=\"tvm\")` now raises `ImportError: Please install apache-tvm to use the tvm backend.`\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  opt = torch.compile(model, backend=\"tvm\", options={\"scheduler\": \"meta_schedule\", \"trials\": 20000})\r\n\r\n  # or through the relay-only entry points\r\n  from torch._dynamo.backends.tvm import tvm_meta_schedule, tvm_auto_scheduler\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n  ```python\r\n  import tvm\r\n\r\n  pipeline = tvm.relax.get_pipeline(\"static_shape_tuning\", target=\"llvm\", total_trials=2000)\r\n  opt = torch.compile(model, backend=\"tvm\", options={\"pipeline\": pipeline})\r\n\r\n  # tvm_meta_schedule / tvm_auto_scheduler no longer exist:\r\n  # ImportError: cannot import name 'tvm_meta_schedule'\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## C++ Frontend\r\n\r\n- Remove the deprecated zero-argument C++ overloads `c10::Scalar::isIntegral()` and `c10::isIntegralType(ScalarType)` (#187115)\r\n\r\n  Code that calls either overload without specifying whether Boolean values count as integral will no longer compile. Pass `includeBool` explicitly; use `false` to preserve the removed overloads' behavior.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  bool scalar_is_integer = scalar.isIntegral();\r\n  bool dtype_is_integer = c10::isIntegralType(dtype);\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  bool scalar_is_integer = scalar.isIntegral(/*includeBool=*/false);\r\n  bool dtype_is_integer =\r\n      c10::isIntegralType(dtype, /*includeBool=*/false);\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Release Engineering\r\n\r\n- `setup.py` is now a deprecation shim; build PyTorch through pip or `python -m build` (#180248)\r\n\r\n  `setup.py` is now a thin shim. `install` and `develop` still forward to pip, but\r\n  `build`, `bdist_wheel`, `clean`, `sdist` and the rest print the replacement\r\n  command instead of falling through to setuptools. Builds that already go through\r\n  a PEP 517 frontend are unaffected, since pip and `python -m build` never ran\r\n  `setup.py`. The shim prints the schedule: `install`/`develop` keep forwarding\r\n  through 2.15, every command stops working in 2.16, and `setup.py` is removed\r\n  in 2.18.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  python setup.py bdist_wheel\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  python -m build --wheel --no-isolation\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## MPS\r\n\r\n- The C++ MPS macOS-version helper and its enum members have been renamed (#188645)\r\n\r\n  Downstream C++ code that includes `<ATen/mps/MPSDevice.h>` must replace the exported `at::mps::is_macos_13_or_newer()` function with `at::mps::is_macos_at_least()`. The associated `MacOSVersion` members also drop the `VER` and `PLUS` portions of their names. No compatibility aliases are provided, so code using the old names will no longer compile.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  const bool supported = at::mps::is_macos_13_or_newer(\r\n      at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_VER_15_0_PLUS);\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  const bool supported = at::mps::is_macos_at_least(\r\n      at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_15_0);\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Complex Frontend\r\n\r\n- Complex type promotion for `bfloat16` now uses the new `torch.bcomplex32` shell dtype instead of `torch.complex64` (#186928)\r\n\r\n  `torch.bcomplex32` stores real and imaginary components as `bfloat16`. Operations that combine a `bfloat16` tensor with a complex scalar or otherwise request its corresponding complex type can therefore produce `bcomplex32` instead of `complex64`. Because `bcomplex32` is a shell dtype with limited operator support, an operation that previously ran in `complex64` may now raise a not-implemented error. Explicitly cast to `complex64` when the previous precision or operator coverage is required.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  x = torch.ones(4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)\r\n  assert torch.result_type(x, 1j) == torch.complex64\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  x = torch.ones(4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)\r\n  assert torch.result_type(x, 1j) == torch.bcomplex32\r\n\r\n  # Preserve the previous complex64 behavior explicitly.\r\n  y = x.to(torch.complex64) + 1j\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n# Deprecations\r\n\r\n## Autograd\r\n\r\n- Selective activation checkpointing will change to honor surrounding `saved_tensors_hooks` by default; use the new `respect_saved_tensors_hooks` argument to choose the behavior explicitly (#190581)\r\n\r\n  The current default, `None`, preserves the legacy behavior in which tensors retained by selective activation checkpointing bypass user hooks, but now emits a `FutureWarning` when hooks are active. Pass `True` to opt into the future behavior or `False` to preserve the legacy behavior without a warning. This option requires `use_reentrant=False`.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack, unpack):\r\n      output = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(\r\n          function,\r\n          input,\r\n          use_reentrant=False,\r\n          context_fn=sac_context_fn,\r\n      )\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack, unpack):\r\n      output = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(\r\n          function,\r\n          input,\r\n          use_reentrant=False,\r\n          context_fn=sac_context_fn,\r\n          respect_saved_tensors_hooks=True,\r\n      )\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n- Use `torch.compiler.config.compile_on_one_rank` instead of `torch.distributed.config.compile_on_one_rank` (#187869)\r\n\r\n  The distributed spelling remains as a forwarding alias but now emits a `FutureWarning`. The preferred environment variable is also `TORCH_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK`; the older `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` remains supported for compatibility.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch.distributed.config\r\n  torch.distributed.config.compile_on_one_rank = True\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch.compiler.config\r\n  torch.compiler.config.compile_on_one_rank = True\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Profiler\r\n\r\n- The experimental `profiler_metrics` and `profiler_measure_per_kernel` options no longer enable CUPTI range profiling and now emit a `FutureWarning` when set to a non-default value (#187204)\r\n\r\n  Kineto no longer supports this range-profiler path on PyTorch's supported CUDA versions. The arguments remain accepted temporarily for compatibility, but they are ignored and have no direct replacement.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  config = torch.profiler._ExperimentalConfig(\r\n      profiler_metrics=[\"sm__cycles_elapsed.avg\"],\r\n      profiler_measure_per_kernel=True,\r\n  )\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  config = torch.profiler._ExperimentalConfig()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- The `with_modules` profiler option is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning` (#192808)\r\n\r\n  `with_modules=True` only collected module hierarchy for TorchScript models and did nothing in eager mode. For eager models, use `with_stack=True` to record `nn.Module` events.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.profiler.profile(with_modules=True) as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch.profiler.profile(with_stack=True) as prof:\r\n      run_workload()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Dynamo\r\n\r\n- `torch._dynamo.config.enable_faithful_generator_behavior` is deprecated and is now a no-op (#189894)\r\n\r\n  Faithful (lazy) generator tracing has been the default and is the only supported behavior, so the dead eager-exhaustion path was removed. The config is kept as a deprecated setting that always behaves as `True`, so setting it does not error but no longer changes anything.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # generators were eagerly exhausted on first execution\r\n  with torch._dynamo.config.patch(enable_faithful_generator_behavior=False):\r\n      torch.compile(fn)(x)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.14:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # the flag is ignored; generators are always traced lazily\r\n  torch.compile(fn)(x)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## CUDA\r\n\r\n- Deprecate `CUDAGraph.register_generator_state()`; CUDA graphs now register generator state lazily on first RNG use during capture (#176753)\r\n\r\n  The method is now a no-op and emits a deprecation warning. Remove explicit registration calls; the graph automatically retains the required state when the generator is used during capture.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\r\n  state = generator.graphsafe_get_state()\r\n  graph.register_generator_state(state)\r\n\r\n  with torch.cuda.graph(graph):\r\n      generator.graphsafe_set_state(state)\r\n      output = torch.rand(16, device=\"cuda\", generator=generator)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()\r\n  state = generator.graphsafe_get_state()\r\n\r\n  with torch.cuda.graph(graph):\r\n      generator.graphsafe_set_state(state)\r\n      output = torch.rand(16, device=\"cuda\", generator=generator)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Deprecate `GreenContext.set_context()` and `GreenContext.pop_context()`; use custom streams to activate a green context instead (#188419)\r\n\r\n  These methods now emit a `FutureWarning`. Create a stream from the green context and use it with `torch.cuda.stream()` instead. Synchronization with streams outside the green context remains the caller's responsibility and should use CUDA events when needed.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  ctx = torch.cuda.green_contexts.GreenContext(num_sms=1)\r\n  ctx.set_context()\r\n  try:\r\n      output = model(input)\r\n  finally:\r\n      ctx.pop_context()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  ctx = torch.cuda.green_contexts.GreenContext(num_sms=1)\r\n  stream = ctx.Stream()\r\n  with torch.cuda.stream(stream):\r\n      output = model(input)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## JIT\r\n\r\n- TorchScript APIs now emit visible `FutureWarning`s instead of normally hidden `DeprecationWarning`s (#189914)\r\n\r\n  Calls such as `torch.jit.script`, `torch.jit.trace`, `torch.jit.save`, and `torch.jit.load` now visibly direct users toward `torch.compile` or `torch.export`. Imports of `torch.utils.mkldnn`, `torch.fx.experimental.optimization`, and `torch.distributed.optim` also avoid eagerly compiling TorchScript when those modules are merely imported.\r\n\r\n  Before:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  scripted = torch.jit.script(model)\r\n  torch.jit.save(scripted, \"model.pt\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  After:\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  exported = torch.export.export(model, example_inputs)\r\n  torch.export.save(exported, \"model.pt2\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n# New Features\r\n\r\n## Python Frontend\r\n\r\n- Add `torch.accelerator.initial_seed()`, `torch.accelerator.get_rng_state()`, and `torch.accelerator.get_rng_state_all()` for backend-agnostic accelerator RNG inspection (#186597)\r\n- Add read-only DLPack export through `Tensor.__dlpack__(read_only=True)` and `torch.utils.dlpack.ReadOnlyTensorWrapper`, including copy-on-write-preserving exchange with compatible consumers (#188554)\r\n- Add `torch.Generator.philox_state()` so Python-authored kernels can reserve Philox counter ranges that remain correct across CUDA Graph capture and replay (#191019)\r\n\r\n## Autograd\r\n\r\n- `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint()` can now be called without a function to create an eager-mode decorator with checkpoint configuration separated from the wrapped function's arguments (#189411)\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  checkpointed_function = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(\r\n      use_reentrant=False\r\n  )(function)\r\n  output = checkpointed_function(*args, **kwargs)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  The curried form is initially supported in eager mode; existing direct calls remain the compatible form under `torch.compile`.\r\n\r\n- Add `torch.autograd.graph.node_creation_hook`, a thread-local context manager whose callback receives every fully populated autograd graph node created within its scope. The callback can inspect nodes, store metadata, or register backward pre-hooks and post-hooks, including for nodes created during higher-order differentiation and checkpoint recomputation (#189284)\r\n\r\n- Add `ctx.set_output_grad_dtype(*dtypes)` for custom `torch.autograd.Function` implementations. Called once from `forward` or `setup_context`, it declares the gradient dtype expected for each output independently of the output's storage dtype; a concrete dtype converts incoming gradients, while `None` leaves their dtype unchanged (#189634)\r\n\r\n- Add second-order gradient support for `torch.cdist` and `torch.nn.functional.pdist`, so grad-grad computations no longer fail because `_cdist_backward` or `_pdist_backward` lacks a derivative (#188901)\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n- Add portable JSON serialization through `DebugMode.save_logs()` and `DebugMode.load_logs()` so backend, which creates per-peer NCCL point-to-point communicators on demand (#189362)\r\n- Add the `CheckpointableTensor` protocol so distributed checkpointing can save and load `torch.Tensor` objects It is available as `from torch._higher_order_ops.switch import switch` and lowers to `torch.ops.higher_order.switch`; autograd is not yet supported (#182902, #188374, #189028)\r\n- Declare dynamic shapes explicitly with `ShapesSpec` / `ParamsSpec`, now accepted by strict and non-strict `torch.export.export`, `make_fx(tracing_mode=\"fake\")`, and `torch.compile` through a shared `dynamic_shapes=` keyword (#185982, #186751, #187602, #187010)\r\n- Support Dynamo and AOTAutograd tracing of permitted input mutations in the prototype `scan`, `map`, and `switch` higher-order ops when gradients are disabled; Inductor lowering for these mutations is not yet supported (#186474, #187568, #188903)\r\n- Support `torch.cuda.use_mem_pool` inside a compiled region, so allocations in the context - including fallback and extern kernels - are routed to the pool (#185057)\r\n- Support calls to `logging.Logger` methods that are explicitly registered in `torch._dynamo.config.reorderable_logging_functions`, so supported positional-argument logging calls run after the compiled region instead of causing graph breaks (#190840)\r\n\r\n## Inductor\r\n\r\n- Add NVGEMM epilogue fusion so supported pointwise operations and output casts can be fused into autotuned matrix multiplications (#186183)\r\n- Add NVGEMM autotuning support for `torch.addmm`, including fused bias and supported pointwise epilogues (#189774)\r\n- Support FlexAttention FLASH-backend backward graphs that differentiate through the returned log-sum-exp output (#189784)\r\n- Add an opt-in `torch._inductor.config.reorder_for_locality_in_training` setting for applying locality-based graph reordering to training graphs (#186643)\r\n- Add opt-in CUDA Graph Trees generation cloning through `torch._inductor.config.triton.cudagraph_trees_generation_cloning = \"user_visible\"`, preserving live user-visible outputs across generations (#188078)\r\n- Add `bfloat16` support to `torch.fft` operations and `torch.stft` on CUDA and add `float16`/`bfloat16` support on XPU. Existing model-container creation and constant-loading paths are unchanged unless external constants are explicitly provided.\r\n\r\n- Support explicit user-defined streams in the AOTInductor C++ wrapper. normalized to rank 4 with a singleton batch dimension before backend selection. This fixes fused execution for rank-3 and vmapped inputs, but automatic backend selection can change floating-point numerics, dropout RNG consumption, whether the result is a view, and higher-order-gradient support. Fused CUDA backends do not support the second derivatives provided by the math backend; code that depends on those semantics should explicitly select the math backend.\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.nn.attention import SDPBackend, sdpa_kernel\r\n\r\n  with sdpa_kernel(backends=[SDPBackend.MATH]):\r\n      output = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(\r\n          query, key, (#186672)\r\n\r\n## Sparse Frontend\r\n\r\n- Always validate sparse-tensor invariants when loading with `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` so malformed checkpoints cannot create tensors whose indices cause out-of-bounds reads (#184750)\r\n\r\n  Validation is an O(nnz) scan and applies regardless of the global `torch.sparse.check_sparse_tensor_invariants` setting. Fix or regenerate malformed sparse checkpoints that now raise errors such as `RuntimeError: size is inconsistent with indices`. Do not use `weights_only=False` as a workaround for untrusted files.\r\n\r\n\r\n# Developers\r\n\r\n## torch.nn\r\n\r\n- Integrate Helion with the native-DSL registry and add reusable kernel PyTorch 2.13.0 Release Notes\r\n\r\n- [Highlights](#highlights)\r\n- [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes)\r\n- [Deprecations](#deprecations)\r\n- [New Features](#new-features)\r\n- [Improvements](#improvements)\r\n- [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes)\r\n- [Performance](#performance)\r\n- [Documentation](#documentation)\r\n- [Developers](#developers)\r\n\r\n# Highlights\r\n\r\n<table>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>FlexAttention</strong> lands on Apple Silicon (MPS), with up to ~12x speedup over SDPA on sparse patterns, and gains a deterministic backward path on CUDA for reproducible gradient computation.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>CuTeDSL \"Native DSL\" backend</strong> gives Inductor a second high-performance code path (alongside Triton) for key GPU operations, with faster compilation. [Prototype]</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong><code>nn.LinearCrossEntropyLoss</code></strong> combines the final prediction and loss computation to cut peak GPU memory by up to 4x for large-vocabulary language model training.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>torchcomms</strong>, a new communications backend for PyTorch Distributed, improves fault tolerance, scalability, and debuggability for large-cluster training.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>FSDP2</strong> now overlaps reduce-scatter and all-gather communications via a dedicated process group (opt-in), increasing distributed training throughput.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>Python 3.15 wheel support</strong> for PyTorch on Linux via the pytorch repository index, including builds compatible with free-threaded 3.15t.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>Broader platform support</strong>: ROCm gains AOTriton 0.12b with native HIP CMake, Arm adds Armv9-A <code>torch.compile</code> targeting, and Intel XPU exposes new device telemetry APIs.</td></tr>\r\n</table>\r\n\r\nFor more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release.\r\n\r\n# Tracked Regressions\r\n\r\n### ROCm wheels break `torch.compile` on CPU in environments without a GPU\r\n\r\nRunning a `torch==2.13.0+rocm7.2` wheel in an environment where no GPU is available (`torch.cuda.is_available()` is `False`) breaks `torch.compile` on the CPU path: the first compile raises `RuntimeError: Can't detect vectorized ISA for CPU` ([#189194](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/189194)). This is a regression from `torch==2.12.1+rocm7.2`, which compiles CPU code fine (detecting e.g. `VecAVX2`) in the same setup. The 2.13 ROCm wheel appears to rely on something present in the ROCm builder image to detect the CPU vectorized ISA, so it works when run on a ROCm image but fails on a plain CPU-only image.\r\n\r\nWorkaround: run the `+rocm` wheel on a ROCm image, or install a standard CPU/CUDA build for GPU-less environments.\r\n\r\n# Backwards Incompatible Changes\r\n\r\n- Stop building CPython 3.13t (free-threaded) binaries (#182951)\r\n\r\n  Upstream `pypa/manylinux` removed CPython 3.13t (free-threaded) on 2026-05-07, because 3.13t\r\n  was experimental and has been superseded by the now-non-experimental CPython 3.14t. As a result,\r\n  PyTorch 2.13 no longer ships `cp313t` wheels (Linux, Triton, and related artifacts). Users on the\r\n  free-threaded interpreter should move to Python 3.14t.\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # cp313t (free-threaded 3.13) wheels were available\r\n  python3.13t -m pip install torch\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Use free-threaded Python 3.14t instead\r\n  python3.14t -m pip install torch\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Bare `PyObject` is no longer allowed in operator schemas (#184209)\r\n\r\n  Bare `PyObject` was accidentally accepted in operator schema strings in\r\n  PyTorch 2.12. This was undocumented and is now rejected, since `torch.compile`\r\n  does not support arbitrary `PyObject` inputs to custom ops. If\r\n  you parse or register a schema with a bare `PyObject` argument or return type,\r\n  you will now get a schema parse error.\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  >>> from torch._C import parse_schema\r\n  >>> parse_schema(\"foo(PyObject x) -> ()\")  # accepted\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  >>> from torch._C import parse_schema\r\n  >>> parse_schema(\"foo(PyObject x) -> ()\")  # raises a schema parse error\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Remove Bazel build support (#180883)\r\n\r\n  The Bazel build was never broadly adopted and still depended on the antiquated Bazel 6,\r\n  while the wider ecosystem has since moved to Bazel 9. All Bazel build files and CI jobs have\r\n  been removed. Users building PyTorch with Bazel should migrate to the supported CMake/`pip install`\r\n  build flow.\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Build PyTorch with Bazel\r\n  bazel build //:torch\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Bazel build files have been removed; build from source with pip instead\r\n  pip install --no-build-isolation -e .\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- `StorageImpl`'s built-in copy-on-write (COW) materialization is replaced by a pluggable materializer hook (#179063)\r\n\r\n  `StorageImpl` no longer knows about COW directly. Its internal COW entry points\r\n  `StorageImpl::is_cow()`, `StorageImpl::maybe_materialize_cow()`, and the friend\r\n  `cow::materialize_cow_storage()` have been removed in favor of a single pluggable\r\n  `MaterializeFn` hook (`void(*)(StorageImpl*)`) that a backend registers to run once,\r\n  on the first mutable data-pointer access. COW is now just one consumer of this hook\r\n  (`c10::impl::cow::materialize_cow`), and all COW behavior (lazy clone, refcounted\r\n  shared data, copy-on-write) is unchanged. This also gives accelerator backends and\r\n  eager-mode graph compilers a zero-fast-path-cost place to commit deferred allocations\r\n  or materialize symbolic buffers on first mutation.\r\n\r\n  This is a C++-only change. It affects out-of-tree backends/extensions that called the\r\n  removed `StorageImpl` COW symbols directly; they will fail to compile against 2.13\r\n  with errors such as `no member named 'is_cow' in 'c10::StorageImpl'`. Migrate to the\r\n  new hook API (`set_materializer()` / `has_materializer()` / `clear_materializer()`).\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  // Detect a COW storage and force it to materialize.\r\n  if (storage.is_cow()) {\r\n    storage.maybe_materialize_cow();\r\n  }\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  // Register a one-shot materializer; it runs on the next mutable-data access\r\n  // and then clears itself. COW registers c10::impl::cow::materialize_cow this way.\r\n  storage.set_materializer(&my_backend_materialize);  // void(StorageImpl*)\r\n\r\n  // `has_materializer()` replaces `is_cow()` for \"is a deferred materialization pending?\"\r\n  if (storage.has_materializer()) { /* ... */ }\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Convert `shared_ptr<Node>` to `intrusive_ptr<Node>` (#181139). This changes the signature of `Tensor::grad_fn`. Accesses to `Tensor.grad_fn()` should change from `std::shared_ptr<Node>` to `c10::intrusive_ptr<Node>`. Similarly, construction of a C++ autograd function should change:\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  std::shared_ptr<CustomCppNode> node(new CustomCppNode(), torch::autograd::deleteNode);\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```cpp\r\n  auto node = c10::make_intrusive<CustomCppNode>();\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- The minimum supported NCCL version when building from source is now 2.23 (#186292)\r\n\r\n  PyTorch now requires NCCL >= 2.23 at compile time, and the preprocessor/runtime gates that guarded NCCL features introduced in 2.23 or earlier have been removed. Users who build PyTorch from source against a system NCCL older than 2.23 will hit compile errors against the dropped gates. Upgrade the NCCL installation to >= 2.23 to build. The prebuilt PyTorch wheels already bundle a compatible NCCL, so pip/conda users are unaffected.\r\n\r\n- Remove named tensors (#173895)\r\n\r\n  The named tensor feature (a long-deprecated prototype) has been fully removed to reduce overhead and code bloat. All associated Python and C++ APIs are gone, including `Tensor.names`, `Tensor.rename()`, `Tensor.refine_names()`, `Tensor.align_to()`, `Tensor.align_as()`, `torch.align_tensors()`, the `names=` keyword on factory functions (e.g. `torch.zeros`, `torch.empty`, `torch.ones`), and the C++ `Dimname` / `DimnameList` APIs. Code that previously relied on named dimensions must track dimension order positionally and avoid usage of any of these now-removed APIs or op overloads.\r\n\r\n- The `onednn::qconv2d_pointwise.binary` and `.binary_tensor` operators no longer alias their input but rather return fresh tensors. Previously these ops mutated the `qaccum` input buffer and returned it directly, violating the PyTorch invariant that custom operator outputs must not alias inputs. This silently bypassed aliasing checks via the old `-> Tensor(a!)` schema and would become a hard error in a future PyTorch version (as mentioned in #182063), so the schema and implementation were corrected to return a fresh output. Most users are unaffected, only code that calls these ops directly and relies on the in-place mutation of qaccum must now read the returned tensor instead. (#177171)\r\n\r\n# Deprecations\r\n\r\n- Custom operators that return an output aliasing one of their inputs are deprecated (#182063)\r\n\r\n  When a custom operator returns an output that is the same tensor as (or otherwise aliases) one of its inputs under `torch.compile`, PyTorch now emits a `UserWarning` stating that this is deprecated and will become an error in a future version of PyTorch. Previously the warning stated the change would land in PyTorch 2.12; that timeline has been pushed back. To update your code, return a clone of the offending output instead of the input, or refactor the operator so it does not return the aliased tensor.\r\n\r\n  Deprecated:\r\n  ```python\r\n  @torch.library.custom_op(\"mylib::foo\", mutates_args=())\r\n  def foo(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\r\n      return x  # output aliases the input -- deprecated\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Updated:\r\n  ```python\r\n  @torch.library.custom_op(\"mylib::foo\", mutates_args=())\r\n  def foo(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\r\n      return x.clone()  # return a clone instead\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Creating tensors with the quantized dtypes `quint8`, `qint8`, and `qint32` is now deprecated and emits a warning. This covers both Python and C++ call sites; see [#184982](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/184982) for migration guidance (#184984)\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  >>> x = torch.quantize_per_tensor(torch.randn(3), 0.1, 0, torch.quint8)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  >>> x = torch.quantize_per_tensor(torch.randn(3), 0.1, 0, torch.quint8)\r\n  UserWarning: Creating tensors with quantized dtypes (quint8, qint8, qint32) is deprecated\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Rename distributed collective ops to the `_single` naming scheme and deprecate the old names (#186123, #186124, #186125, #186134, #186135, #186144)\r\n\r\n  To align the public `torch.distributed` collective APIs with the naming used by torchcomms' `TorchCommBackend`, `all_gather_into_tensor` is renamed to `all_gather_single` and `reduce_scatter_tensor` to `reduce_scatter_single`. The previous names continue to work as thin wrappers that delegate to the new functions, but now emit a `FutureWarning`.\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  dist.all_gather_into_tensor(output, input)\r\n  dist.reduce_scatter_tensor(output, input)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  PyTorch 2.13:\r\n  ```python\r\n  dist.all_gather_single(output, input)\r\n  dist.reduce_scatter_single(output, input)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n# New Features\r\n\r\n## Python Frontend\r\n\r\n- Add two new operator tags, `torch.Tag.inplace` and `torch.Tag.out`, that let an operator declare how it writes its result: `inplace` means it mutates a tensor in place, and `out` means it writes into a caller-provided output tensor. Native PyTorch operators are tagged automatically, and custom operators defined with `torch.library` can opt in by adding the tag. To be tagged `inplace`, an operator must take the tensor it mutates as its first positional argument (declared as `Tensor(a!)`, and the only mutable argument) and return that same tensor. Tagging a custom operator this way improves its behavior under `torch.compile`: `inplace` ops now go through `auto_functionalize`, so the reinplacing pass can analyze clones and skip unnecessary copies, and both `inplace` and `out` ops get their fake/meta kernels generated for free. See the [Python custom operators tutorial](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/advanced/python_custom_ops.html) for how to author and tag custom operators. (#181100, #181099, #184199, #184200, #184201, #184202, #184203, #180851, #180852)\r\n- Add `const_data_ptr()` Python binding to `torch.Tensor` for read-only data pointer access (#180382)\r\n- Add an `abbr` property to `torch.dtype` that returns a dtype's short string abbreviation (e.g. `torch.float32.abbr` returns `\"f32\"`) (#177296)\r\n- Allow positional arguments to be passed as keyword arguments to autograd custom `Function`s (#182206)\r\n- Expose `rearrange` in the `torch.func` namespace for einops-style tensor reshaping (#173183)\r\n\r\n## torch.nn\r\n\r\n- Add `nn.LinearCrossEntropyLoss`, a fused linear-projection plus cross-entropy loss module that avoids materializing the full logits tensor (#181573, #185852, #172286, #186113)\r\n\r\n## Autograd\r\n\r\n- Add `torch.autograd.graph.region_activation_memory_budget` (#185979)\r\n- Support passing gradient inputs as a `dict` to `torch.autograd.grad` and `torch.autograd.backward` (#178140)\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n- Add a registration API for symmetric memory arguments (`lib.register_symm_mem_args()`), letting operators (including out-of-tree ops) declare which arguments require symmetric-memory allocation (#173513)\r\n- Remove `NCCLSymmetricMemory`'s explicit dependency on `ProcessGroupNCCL`, enabling symmetric memory to work with out-of-tree backends such as torchcomms PyTorch 2.12.0 Release Notes\r\n\r\n- [Highlights](#highlights)\r\n- [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes)\r\n- [Deprecations](#deprecations)\r\n- [New [Security](#security)\r\n\r\n# Highlights\r\n\r\n<table>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>Batched linalg.eigh on CUDA</strong> is up to 100x faster due to updated cuSolver backend selection.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td>New <strong>torch.accelerator.Graph</strong> API unifies graph capture and replay across CUDA, XPU, and out-of-tree backends.</td></tr>\r\n  <tr><td><strong>torch.export.save</strong> now <tr><td><strong>ROCm</strong> users gain expandable memory segments, rocSHMEM symmetric memory collectives, and FlexAttention pipelining.</td></tr>\r\n</table>\r\n\r\nFor more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release.\r\n\r\n# Backwards Incompatible Changes\r\n\r\n## Build Frontend\r\n\r\n- Strengthened SVE compile checks in `FindARM.cmake`, which may reject previously accepted but incorrect SVE configurations ([#176646](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/176646))\r\n\r\n  Source builds that enable SVE now validate the compiler configuration more strictly. If a build previously passed with an incomplete or mismatched SVE setup, it may now fail during CMake configuration instead of later in compilation. Update the compiler/toolchain flags so they accurately describe the target SVE support, or disable SVE for that build.\r\n\r\n- Updated the minimum CUDA version required to build PyTorch from source to CUDA 12.6 ([#178925](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/178925))\r\n\r\n  Building PyTorch from source with CUDA versions older than 12.6 is no longer supported. Users building custom binaries should install CUDA 12.6 or newer and make sure `CUDA_HOME` points to that installation.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.4 python setup.py develop\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.6 python setup.py develop\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- Enforced a C++20 minimum in CMake build files ([#178662](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/178662))\r\n\r\n  Source builds now require a compiler and build configuration that support C++20. If you maintain custom build scripts or downstream extensions that build PyTorch from source, update the compiler and remove assumptions that PyTorch can be built as C++17.\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n- `torch.distributed.nn.functional` ops now raise `RuntimeError` under `torch.compile` ([#177342](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177342))\r\n\r\n  All ops in `torch.distributed.nn.functional` (e.g., `broadcast`, `all_reduce`, `all_gather`, `reduce_scatter`, `all_to_all_single`) now raise `RuntimeError` when called inside `torch.compile`. Users should migrate to the functional collectives API in `torch.distributed._functional_collectives`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  @torch.compile\r\n  def my_func(x):\r\n      return torch.distributed.nn.functional.all_reduce(x, op=ReduceOp.SUM)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  @torch.compile\r\n  def my_func(x):\r\n      return torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_reduce(x, reduceOp=\"sum\", group=group)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## TorchElastic\r\n\r\n- `torchrun` now defaults to an OS-assigned free port for single-node training instead of port 29500 ([#175699](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/175699))\r\n\r\n  When running `torchrun --nproc-per-node=N script.py` without specifying `--master-port` or `--standalone`, the default behavior now automatically uses an OS-assigned free port via the `c10d` rendezvous backend. This eliminates \"Address already in use\" errors when running multiple training jobs concurrently. Multi-node training, explicit `--master-port`, `PET_MASTER_PORT` env var, and `--standalone` are unchanged.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Used static rendezvous on port 29500 by default\r\n  torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 train.py\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Uses OS-assigned free port by default\r\n  torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 train.py\r\n\r\n  # To explicitly use a fixed port:\r\n  torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 --master-port=29500 train.py\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## MPS\r\n\r\n- All MPS tensors are now allocated in unified memory ([#175818](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/175818))\r\n\r\n  Previously, MPS tensors could be allocated in either device-only or unified memory. Now all MPS tensors use unified memory unconditionally. This simplifies memory management and enables CPU access to MPS tensor data without explicit copies. Code that relied on device-only memory placement may observe different performance characteristics.\r\n\r\n## Inductor\r\n\r\n- The `max_autotune` layout-constraint deferral introduced in 2.11 is now opt-in ([#175330](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/175330))\r\n\r\n  In 2.11, Inductor deferred layout freezing for `max_autotune` templates to expose more fusion opportunities. This caused a regional-inductor failure mode, so the default in 2.12 reverts to immediate layout freezing. Users who relied on the deferred behavior for fusion opportunities should opt in explicitly via `torch._inductor.config.max_autotune_defer_layout_freezing` or `TORCHINDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE_DEFER_LAYOUT_FREEZING=1`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Deferred layout freezing was the default\r\n  torch.compile(model, mode=\"max-autotune\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch._inductor.config as cfg\r\n  cfg.max_autotune_defer_layout_freezing = True\r\n  # or set TORCHINDUCTOR_MAX_AUTOTUNE_DEFER_LAYOUT_FREEZING=1\r\n  torch.compile(model, mode=\"max-autotune\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n# Deprecations\r\n\r\n## Release Engineering\r\n\r\n- Deprecate CUDA 12.8 builds in favor of CUDA 13.0 ([#179072](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/179072))\r\n\r\n  CUDA 12.8 binaries have been removed from the PyTorch binary build matrix. CUDA 13.0 is now the stable default and CUDA 12.6 remains available for users on older drivers. Users explicitly pinning the `cu128` index URL will need to switch to `cu130` (recommended) or `cu126`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # Use CUDA 13.0 (default on PyPI):\r\n  pip install torch\r\n  # Or explicitly:\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130\r\n  # Older driver fallback:\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126\r\n  ```\r\n- Compatibility with CMake < 3.10 will be removed in a future release ([#166259](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/166259))\r\n\r\n  Source builds against CMake versions older than 3.10 now emit a deprecation warning. A future release will require CMake 3.10 or newer; please upgrade CMake before then.\r\n\r\n## Linear Algebra\r\n\r\n- Several CUDA linear algebra operators no longer use the MAGMA backend and now dispatch to cuSolver or cuBLAS unconditionally:\r\n  - `torch.linalg.eigh` now dispatches to cuSolver ([#174619](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174619))\r\n  - `torch.linalg.lu_solve` now dispatches to cuSolver/cuBLAS ([#174248](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174248))\r\n  - `torch.linalg.cholesky_inverse` now dispatches to cuSolver ([#174681](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174681))\r\n  - `torch.linalg.cholesky_solve` now dispatches to cuSolver ([#174769](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174769))\r\n\r\n  User code calling these APIs does not need to change. The practical impact is for users who depended on MAGMA-specific numerical behavior, performance characteristics, or debugging. Those calls now use the cuSolver/cuBLAS implementations on CUDA.\r\n\r\n## FullyShardedDataParallel2 (FSDP2)\r\n\r\n- Compiling through FSDP2 hooks without graph breaks is no longer supported ([#174863](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174863), [#174906](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174906)). If you use compiled autograd with FSDP2, update your code to allow graph breaks around FSDP2 hooks or disable compiled autograd for the FSDP2 training step.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  with torch._dynamo.config.patch(compiled_autograd=True):\r\n      compiled_model = torch.compile(fsdp_model, fullgraph=True)\r\n      loss = compiled_model(input).sum()\r\n      loss.backward()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Either run FSDP2 backward without fullgraph.\r\n  compiled_model = torch.compile(fsdp_model, fullgraph=False)\r\n  loss = compiled_model(input).sum()\r\n  loss.backward()\r\n\r\n  # Or apply compile before applying FSDP.\r\n  compiled_model_pre_fsdp = torch.compile(model, fullgraph=True)\r\n  compiled_model = fully_shard(compiled_model_pre_fsdp, ...)\r\n  loss = compiled_model(input).sum()\r\n  loss.backward()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Profiler\r\n\r\n- Profiler's `metadata_json` field is now deprecated; use `event_metadata` instead ([#179417](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/179417))\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  metadata = event.metadata_json\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  metadata = event.event_metadata\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Dynamo\r\n\r\n- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` now warns when a call runs no compiled code; will error in 2.13 ([#181940](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/181940))\r\n\r\n  Previously `fullgraph=True` was only validated once Dynamo actually compiled and ran the function. If Dynamo was bypassed at call time (e.g. under a user-defined `TorchDispatchMode`), the annotation silently had no effect. 2.12 emits a warning; **2.13 will raise.** For graph-break errors without `fullgraph`'s stronger guarantees, use `torch._dynamo.error_on_graph_break`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode\r\n\r\n  class LoggingMode(TorchDispatchMode):\r\n      def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):\r\n          return func(*args, **(kwargs or {}))\r\n\r\n  @torch.compile(fullgraph=True)\r\n  def model(x):\r\n      return x.sin() + 1\r\n\r\n  # A user-defined TorchDispatchMode is active, so Dynamo skips the frame\r\n  # and no compiled code runs — emits a warning in 2.12, will raise in 2.13.\r\n  with LoggingMode(): # Remove this to fix warning\r\n      model(torch.randn(3, 4))\r\n\r\n  ```\r\n- The `inline_inbuilt_nn_modules` Dynamo config is deprecated ([#177489](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177489), [#178205](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/178205))\r\n\r\n  Inlining of in-built `nn.Module` instances is now the default; setting the flag emits a deprecation warning and it will be removed in a future release.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  import torch._dynamo.config as cfg\r\n  cfg.inline_inbuilt_nn_modules = True  # was a tunable knob\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.12:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # No action needed — inlining is on by default.\r\n  # Remove any explicit references to torch._dynamo.config.inline_inbuilt_nn_modules.\r\n  ```\r\n- Added a deprecation framework to the `torch.compile` config module so individual options can be marked deprecated ([#169837](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/169837))\r\n\r\n# New Features\r\n\r\n## Release Engineering\r\n\r\n- Add Claude-powered autorevert AI advisor workflow Inductor now codegens stream context managers (enter/exit) and `record_stream` calls in the wrapper, enabling user streams to flow through compiled regions with proper synchronization, scheduler integration, and cross-stream dependency tracking ([#165390](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/165390), [#165391](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/165391), [#165504](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/165504), [#165505](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/165505), [#174223](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/174223), [#176700](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/176700), [#177694](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177694))\r\n- Added `ao::offload`, `ao::reload`, and `ao::wait` ops for asynchronous activation offloading. These ops encapsulate async CPU offloading stream management following the same async 2-op pattern as c10d functional collectives, reducing IR size from 7 nodes (offload) and 5 nodes (reload) down to 2 nodes each ([#177621](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177621))\r\n- Added user-defined Triton kernel unary epilogue fusion. persistent Triton templates for `mm` and `addmm` for max-autotune, enabling persistent kernels on hardware without TMA ([#177781](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177781), Below are the full release notes for this release.\r\n\r\n# Backwards Incompatible Changes\r\n\r\n## Release Engineering\r\n\r\n### Volta (SM 7.0) GPU support removed from CUDA 12.8 and 12.9 binary builds (#172598)\r\n\r\n  Starting with PyTorch 2.11, the CUDA 12.8 and 12.9 pre-built binaries no longer include support for Volta GPUs (compute capability 7.0, e.g. V100). This change was necessary to enable updating to CuDNN 9.15.1, which is incompatible with Volta.\r\n\r\n  Users with Volta GPUs who need CUDA 12.8+ should use the CUDA 12.6 builds, which continue to include Volta support. Alternatively, build PyTorch from source with Volta included in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```\r\n  # CUDA 12.8 builds supported Volta (SM 7.0)\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128\r\n  # Works on V100\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```\r\n  # CUDA 12.8 builds no longer support Volta\r\n  # For V100 users, use CUDA 12.6 builds instead:\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n### PyPI wheels now ship with CUDA 13.0 instead of CUDA 12.x ([#172663](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/172663), [announcement](https://dev-discuss.pytorch.org/t/transitioning-pypi-cuda-wheels-to-cuda-13-0-as-the-stable-release-2-11/3325))\r\n\r\n  Starting with PyTorch 2.11, `pip install torch` on PyPI installs CUDA 13.0 wheels by default for both Linux x86_64 and Linux aarch64. Previously, PyPI wheels shipped with CUDA 12.x and only Linux x86_64 CUDA wheels were available on PyPI. Users whose systems have only CUDA 12.x drivers installed may encounter errors when running `pip install torch` without specifying an index URL.\r\n\r\n  Additionally, CUDA 13.0 only supports Turing (SM 7.5) and newer GPU architectures on Linux x86_64. Maxwell and Pascal GPUs are no longer supported under CUDA 13.0. Users with these older GPUs should use the CUDA 12.6 builds instead.\r\n\r\n  CUDA 12.6 and 12.8 binaries remain available via `download.pytorch.org`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # PyPI wheel used CUDA 12.x\r\n  pip install torch\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```bash\r\n  # PyPI wheel now uses CUDA 13.0\r\n  pip install torch\r\n\r\n  # To get CUDA 12.8 wheels instead:\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128\r\n\r\n  # To get CUDA 12.6 wheels (includes Maxwell/Pascal/Volta support):\r\n  pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Python Frontend\r\n\r\n### `torch.hub.list()`, `torch.hub.load()`, and `torch.hub.help()` now default the `trust_repo` parameter to `\"check\"` instead of `None`. The `trust_repo=None` option has been removed. (#174101)\r\n\r\n  Previously, passing `trust_repo=None` (or relying on the default) would silently download and run code from untrusted repositories with only a warning. Now, the default `\"check\"` behavior will prompt the user for explicit confirmation before running code from repositories not on the trusted list.\r\n\r\n  Users who were explicitly passing `trust_repo=None` must update their code. Users who were already passing `trust_repo=True`, `trust_repo=False`, or `trust_repo=\"check\"` are not affected.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Default trust_repo=None — downloads with a warning\r\n  torch.hub.load(\"user/repo\", \"model\")\r\n  # Explicit None — same behavior\r\n  torch.hub.load(\"user/repo\", \"model\", trust_repo=None)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Default trust_repo=\"check\" — prompts for confirmation if repo is not trusted\r\n  torch.hub.load(\"user/repo\", \"model\")\r\n  # To skip the prompt, explicitly trust the repo\r\n  torch.hub.load(\"user/repo\", \"model\", trust_repo=True)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## torch.nn\r\n\r\n### Add sliding window support to `varlen_attn` via `window_size`, making optional arguments keyword-only (#172238)\r\n\r\n  The signature of `torch.nn.attention.varlen_attn` has changed: a `*` (keyword-only separator) has been inserted before the optional arguments. Previously, optional arguments like `is_causal`, `return_aux`, and `scale` could be passed positionally; they must now be passed as keyword arguments. A new `window_size` keyword argument has also been added.\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Before (2.10)\r\n  output = varlen_attn(query, key, value, cu_seq_q, cu_seq_k, max_q, max_k, True, None, 1.0)\r\n\r\n  # After (2.11) — pass as keyword argument\r\n  output = varlen_attn(query, key, value, cu_seq_q, cu_seq_k, max_q, max_k, window_size=(-1, 0), return_aux=None, scale=1.0)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n### Remove `is_causal` flag from `varlen_attn` (#172245)\r\n\r\n  The `is_causal` parameter has been removed from `torch.nn.attention.varlen_attn`. Causal attention is now expressed through the `window_size` parameter: use `window_size=(-1, 0)` for causal masking, or `window_size=(W, 0)` for causal attention with a sliding window of size `W`. The default `window_size=(-1, -1)` corresponds to full (non-causal) attention.\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Before (2.10)\r\n  output = varlen_attn(query, key, value, cu_seq_q, cu_seq_k, max_q, max_k, is_causal=True)\r\n\r\n  # After (2.11) — use window_size instead\r\n  output = varlen_attn(query, key, value, cu_seq_q, cu_seq_k, max_q, max_k, window_size=(-1, 0))\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n### `DebugInfoWriter` now honors `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` for its cache directory in C++ code, consistent with the Python side. Previously it always used `~/.cache/torch`. (#168232)\r\n\r\n  This avoids issues where `$HOME` is not set or not writable. Users who relied on `~/.cache/torch` being used regardless of `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` may see debug info written to a different location.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```\r\n  # C++ DebugInfoWriter always wrote to ~/.cache/torch\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```\r\n  # C++ DebugInfoWriter now respects $XDG_CACHE_HOME/torch (same as Python code)\r\n  # Falls back to ~/.cache/torch if $XDG_CACHE_HOME is not set\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n### `DeviceMesh` now stores a process group registry (`_pg_registry`) directly, enabling `torch.compile` to trace through `get_group()`. (#172272)\r\n\r\n  This may break code that skips `init_process_group`, loads a saved DTensor (constructing a DeviceMesh with no PGs), and later creates PGs separately — during `torch.compile` runtime the PG lookup will fail. Users should ensure process groups are initialized before constructing the DeviceMesh.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # PGs resolved via global _resolve_process_group at runtime\r\n  mesh = DeviceMesh(...)  # PGs could be created later\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # PGs now stored on DeviceMesh._pg_registry; must exist at mesh creation\r\n  dist.init_process_group(...)  # Must be called before creating mesh\r\n  mesh = DeviceMesh(...)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Distributed (DTensor)\r\n\r\n### `DTensor.to_local()` backward now converts `Partial` placements to `Replicate` by default when `grad_placements` is not provided. (#173454)\r\n\r\n  Previously, calling `to_local()` on a `Partial` DTensor would preserve the `Partial` placement in the backward gradient, which could produce incorrect gradients when combined with `from_local()`. Now, the backward pass automatically maps `Partial` forward placements to `Replicate` gradient placements, matching the behavior of `from_local()`.\r\n\r\n  Users who relied on the previous behavior (where `to_local()` backward preserved `Partial` gradients) may see different gradient values. To ensure correctness, explicitly pass `grad_placements` to `to_local()`.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Partial placement preserved in backward — could produce incorrect gradients\r\n  local_tensor = partial_dtensor.to_local()\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Partial → Replicate in backward by default (correct behavior)\r\n  local_tensor = partial_dtensor.to_local()\r\n  # Or explicitly specify grad_placements for full control:\r\n  local_tensor = partial_dtensor.to_local(grad_placements=[Replicate()])\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n### `_PhiloxState.seed` and `_PhiloxState.offset` now return `torch.Tensor` instead of `int` (#173876)\r\n\r\n  The DTensor RNG internal `_PhiloxState` class changed its `seed` and `offset` properties to return tensors instead of Python ints, and the setters now expect tensors. This makes the RNG state compatible with PT2 tracing (the previous `.item()` calls were not fake-tensor friendly).\r\n\r\n  Code that directly reads `_PhiloxState.seed` or `_PhiloxState.offset` and treats them as ints will break. Call `.item()` to get the int value. When setting, wrap the value in a tensor.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.distributed.tensor._random import _PhiloxState\r\n\r\n  philox = _PhiloxState(state)\r\n  seed: int = philox.seed          # returned int\r\n  philox.offset = 42               # accepted int\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.distributed.tensor._random import _PhiloxState\r\n\r\n  philox = _PhiloxState(state)\r\n  seed: int = philox.seed.item()   # now returns Tensor; call .item() for int\r\n  philox.offset = torch.tensor([42], dtype=torch.int64)  # must pass Tensor\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## ROCm\r\n\r\n### caffe2 support is fully removed from ROCm PyTorch's hipify preprocessing. This is known as \"hipify v2\" behavior. (#174087, #174300, #174388, #174499, #175098)\r\n#### hipify v1 background\r\nWhen caffe2 and PyTorch were separate projects, the ROCm support strategies were different.  For caffe2, all files and classes would be renamed following the pattern of CUDA to HIP, Cuda to Hip, cuda to hip, and so on.  PyTorch did not rename classes, but would create new files following the same renaming pattern (e.g., aten/src/ATen/cuda/CUDABlas.h to aten/src/ATen/hip/HIPBlas.h).  As a consequence, caffe2 had a distinct device backend named \"HIP\" (renamed from \"CUDA\") while ROCm PyTorch masquerades as the \"cuda\" device (`torch.empty(1, device=\"cuda\")`).  Once caffe2 and PyTorch projects were merged, this caused a mismatch between caffe2 expecting to use a \"HIP\" device while PyTorch expecting a \"cuda\" device.  To alleviate this mismatch, \"Masquerading\" classes were created under aten/src/ATen/hip/impl.\r\n- HIPAllocatorMasqueradingAsCUDA.h\r\n- HIPCachingAllocatorMasqueradingAsCUDA.h\r\n- HIPGuardImplMasqueradingAsCUDA.h\r\n- HIPStreamMasqueradingAsCUDA.h\r\nThese classes were often transparently utilized during ROCm PyTorch's hipify preprocessing of source files.  All files under c10/ and caffe2/ were hipified using the caffe2 renaming behavior, while all other \"PyTorch\" files used the other strategy.  The Masquerading classes would replace their CUDA counterpart during hipify preprocessing.  For example, c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h's CUDAStream would be replaced by aten/src/ATen/hip/impl/HIPStreamMasqueradingAsCUDA.h's HIPStreamMasqueradingAsCUDA.  These Masquerading classes call the underlying caffe2 code and create \"HIP\" devices, and the device would be reset to \"cuda\" by the Masquerading classes.\r\n#### hipify v2 new behavior\r\nHipify v2 (#174087, #174300, #174388, #174499, #175098) makes the following changes:\r\n- \"Masquerading\" classes are deprecated. Reworked to be thin shells around existing classes, for backward compatibility.\r\n- Do not rename \"CUDA\" classes to \"HIP\". Only rename CUDA Runtime APIs. Files are still renamed out of place.\r\n- Removes caffe2 work-arounds for HIP device versus CUDA device.\r\nGreat care has been taken to make this change backwards compatible.  Though PyTorch today builds cleanly using hipify v2 behavior, downstream PyTorch extension projects that explicitly included Masquerading headers or called Masquerading APIs could be affected, resulting in failed builds.  As an example, before backwards compatibility was realized, the xformers project had failed to build using the hipify v2 changes.  A [PR demonstrates the changes that were initially necessary to work around the build failures,](https://github.com/facebookresearch/xformers/pull/1351) but such changes are no longer necessary after hipify v2 BC-breaking behavior was improved.\r\n\r\n## torch.export\r\n\r\n### `torch.export.export_for_training` has been removed (#171714)\r\n\r\n  `export_for_training` was previously available as a separate API for exporting models while preserving training semantics. This function has been removed. Users should use `torch.export.export` instead, which returns the same graph as the previous `export_for_training`.\r\n\r\n## ONNX\r\n\r\n### **Remove the `fallback` option from `torch.onnx.export`** (#173189)\r\n\r\n  The `fallback` parameter has been removed from `torch.onnx.export()`. Previously, when `fallback=True`, the exporter would automatically fall back to the legacy TorchScript-based exporter if the dynamo exporter failed. This fallback was removed because it was overly complicated, required different inputs, produced different models, and hid errors from the new exporter.\r\n\r\n  **Migration:** Remove `fallback=True` (or `fallback=False`) from your `torch.onnx.export()` calls. If you need fallback behavior, implement it explicitly in your own code by catching exceptions and calling the legacy exporter separately.\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Before\r\n  torch.onnx.export(model, args, \"model.onnx\", dynamo=True, fallback=True)\r\n\r\n  # After\r\n  torch.onnx.export(model, args, \"model.onnx\", dynamo=True)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n### **Remove overload matching logic from the ONNX dispatcher** (#165083)\r\n\r\n  The `custom_translation_table` parameter in `torch.onnx.export()` no longer accepts a list of functions for each torch op. Previously, users could pass a list of overloaded ONNX functions (e.g., one for float tensors, another for bool tensors), and the dispatcher would automatically select the correct overload based on input types. This complex type-matching logic has been removed because torchlib no longer uses overloads for the same opset version.\r\n\r\n  The type of `custom_translation_table` changed from `dict[Callable, Callable | Sequence[Callable]]` to `dict[Callable, Callable]`. Passing a `Sequence` as a value now raises a `TypeError`.\r\n\r\n  **Migration:** Provide a single function per operator instead of a list of overloads. If you need type-dependent behavior, handle it inside the single function.\r\n\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Before\r\n  custom_translation_table = {\r\n      torch.ops.aten.logical_and.default: [custom_impl_float, custom_impl_bool],\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  # After\r\n  custom_translation_table = {\r\n      torch.ops.aten.logical_and.default: custom_impl,\r\n  }\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Quantization\r\n\r\n### The PT2E quantization flow (`torch.ao.quantization.pt2e` and `torch.ao.quantization.quantizer`) has been removed from PyTorch and migrated to [torchao](https://github.com/pytorch/ao). (#169151)\r\n\r\n  The following modules and classes have been removed:\r\n  - `torch.ao.quantization.pt2e` (including `DuplicateDQPass`, `PortNodeMetaForQDQ`, export utils, graph utils, numeric debugger, lowering utilities)\r\n  - `torch.ao.quantization.quantizer` (including `ComposableQuantizer`, `EmbeddingQuantizer`, `X86InductorQuantizer`, `XPUInductorQuantizer`, `XNNPACKQuantizer`, `QuantizationSpec`, `QuantizationAnnotation`, `QuantizationConfig`, etc.)\r\n\r\n  Users relying on the PT2E quantization flow should migrate to the `torchao` package, which now hosts these APIs.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.ao.quantization.pt2e import prepare_pt2e, convert_pt2e\r\n  from torch.ao.quantization.quantizer.x86_inductor_quantizer import X86InductorQuantizer\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Install torchao: pip install torchao\r\n  from torchao.quantization.pt2e import prepare_pt2e, convert_pt2e\r\n  from torchao.quantization.pt2e.quantizer.x86_inductor_quantizer import X86InductorQuantizer\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n\r\n# Deprecations\r\n\r\n## Linear Algebra\r\n\r\n- The MAGMA backend for linear algebra operations is now deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Setting `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")` or retrieving a previously-set MAGMA preference will now issue a deprecation warning. cuSOLVER remains the default backend. (#172823)\r\n\r\n  If you see any errors when using cuSOLVER that did not occur with MAGMA, please file an issue on GitHub. To silence the warning, stop explicitly selecting the MAGMA backend:\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # No warning\r\n  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # Issues a deprecation warning — remove this call to use the default cuSOLVER backend\r\n  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- `torch.linalg.svd` no longer dispatches to MAGMA. The MAGMA backend is deprecated and cuSOLVER is now used unconditionally, providing significant speedups (2x–400x depending on matrix size and batch dimensions). (#172824)\r\n\r\n  Previously, setting `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")` would route SVD through MAGMA. This setting is now ignored for SVD, and cuSOLVER is always used.\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")\r\n  U, S, Vh = torch.linalg.svd(x)  # Uses MAGMA\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # MAGMA preference is ignored; cuSOLVER is always used\r\n  U, S, Vh = torch.linalg.svd(x)  # Uses cuSOLVER\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- `torch.linalg.solve_triangular` and `torch.triangular_solve` no longer dispatch to MAGMA on CUDA. cuBLAS is now used unconditionally, providing speedups of 2x–24x for most matrix sizes (small matrices may see minor regressions of ~0.6x). (#174109)\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")\r\n  torch.linalg.solve_triangular(A, B, upper=False)  # Uses MAGMA\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # MAGMA preference is ignored; cuBLAS is always used\r\n  torch.linalg.solve_triangular(A, B, upper=False)  # Uses cuBLAS\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n- `torch.linalg.lstsq` no longer dispatches to MAGMA. cuSOLVER/cuBLAS are now used unconditionally, providing speedups of 1.7x–620x depending on matrix size and batch dimensions. (#174779)\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library(\"magma\")\r\n  result = torch.linalg.lstsq(A, B)  # Uses MAGMA\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # MAGMA preference is ignored; cuSOLVER/cuBLAS is always used\r\n  result = torch.linalg.lstsq(A, B)  # Uses cuSOLVER/cuBLAS\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n## Distributed\r\n\r\n### `torch.distributed.symmetric_memory.enable_symm_mem_for_group` is deprecated. The store can be retrieved directly via `ProcessGroup.getStore()` in C++, making this call unnecessary. (#172163)\r\n\r\n  Version 2.10:\r\n  ```python\r\n  from torch.distributed.symmetric_memory import enable_symm_mem_for_group\r\n  enable_symm_mem_for_group(group)\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n  Version 2.11:\r\n  ```python\r\n  # No longer needed — store is accessed directly from the ProcessGroup\r\n  ```\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n# New features\r\n\r\n## Python Frontend\r\n- Added `native_handle` property to `torch.Stream`, providing a unified way to retrieve the backend-specific opaque stream handle (e.g., `cudaStream_t` for CUDA, `sycl::queue*` for XPU). PyTorch 2.10.0 Release Notes\r\n\r\n- [Highlights](#highlights)\r\n- [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes)\r\n- [Deprecations](#deprecations)\r\n- [New
